chapter: Learning from players; Jonah Jones lessons
title: Ben Webster fitting solos into the section
summary: Webster's solos came out of and back into the arrangement.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: I'll just mention this one thing about

Ben, I wonder if you ever noticed this. Having worked with Ben in the band with Ben, and worked with Chu Berry and other great saxophone players, Ben Webster would play his solos so that he came out of his part, into his solo. And at the end of his solo he didn't just say the hell with it, it's all over, he had some sort of little innovation that put him right back down into his part again, which made me feel he always had respect for his section.

And always believed in that, and that's true, he did. I noticed that because I have always believed that when you played in a big band, especially, your solo is part of a big arrangement and it should fit the background and it should come out of what went before and lead into what follows. I am a very strong believer in that. And that was one of the things that bothered me in the years after the swing era, was the total disregard that soloists would have for the context of their solos.
Thank you for that, Jim. I'm glad you and I agree on that.
